papers.title: CUAWright: A Minimal Unified Interface for Digital Agents
papers.problem: Computer-use agents rely on fixed screen tools, so they cannot build their own tools or run code directly.
papers.fix: A bash-only terminal agent gained 33.2% partial reward and cut cost 37.5% on OSWorld 2.0.
papers.practicalUseCase: Screen clicking may be the wrong way to drive a computer, so give your agent a terminal first.
papers.limitation: Gains come from benchmark tests, so daily real-world results may differ.

papers.title: JEPA-TTT: Persistent Test-Time Training of Latent World Models for Planning under Dynamics Shifts
papers.problem: Planning models give bad predictions when the world behaves differently at test time than in training.
papers.fix: Updating the model during use cut prediction error by 83% and raised planning performance by 153% after 500 episodes.
papers.practicalUseCase: A frozen model decays when conditions change, so let it keep learning from its own experience.
papers.limitation: Tests covered eight changes in four control environments, not messy real-world systems.

papers.title: WM-VLM: Probing Internal World Models for Interleaved Visual-Textual Reasoning
papers.problem: Vision-language models reason mostly in words, so they struggle with spatial puzzles that people solve by picturing shapes.
papers.fix: Letting the model draw its own intermediate pictures raised mental rotation scores by up to 39.25 percentage points.
papers.practicalUseCase: Models that picture each step solve spatial tasks better, so pick image-generating reasoning for spatial work.
papers.limitation: Tests used programmatically built rotation puzzles, so results may not carry to real photos.

papers.title: Improving Atomic-Fact Recall via Focused Views in Unstructured Knowledge Editing
papers.problem: Edited language models can repeat the new passage but fail to recall its separate facts without it.
papers.fix: Randomly shifting position values during editing improved fact recall across five editors, two models, and three benchmarks.
papers.practicalUseCase: Model updates can look successful but still lose facts, so test recall of each fact, not the whole passage.
papers.limitation: The method only covers two model families and edit methods that use rotary position encoding.

papers.title: PointWAM: 3D World Action Modeling for Dexterous Robotic Manipulation
papers.problem: Robot models that predict flat images or joint angles miss the 3D shape and contact needed for hand tasks.
papers.fix: Predicting scene and hand motion as 3D points beat the prior best by 11.7 points on ten tasks.
papers.practicalUseCase: Human videos can teach robot hands, since pre-training on them added 56.9 points, so reuse that footage.
papers.limitation: Results come from the DexJoCo simulation tasks plus one real robot, so wider claims need more tests.

papers.title: Sustainability Committees and Environmental Initiatives: Insights from Dual Banking Systems in Emerging Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Banks set up sustainability committees, but nobody knew whether they improve environmental results in Islamic and conventional banks.
papers.fix: Committees linked to better environmental scores, but in Islamic banks they did not link to green products or innovation.
papers.practicalUseCase: Committees may show symbolic effort in Islamic banks, so check for real green products before trusting a bank's claims.
papers.limitation: Panel regressions show links, not cause, and cover only emerging-market banks.

papers.title: Trends and Determinants of Sustainability Sukuk Issuance: Evidence from Global Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Sustainability sukuk are growing, but nobody knew what drives how large each issue is.
papers.fix: Across 11,944 sukuk issues from 2012 to 2022, equity-based contracts, strong security, and USD or Euro currency gave larger issues.
papers.practicalUseCase: Issuers who want bigger sustainability sukuk should choose equity-based contracts and major currencies, and skip costly second-party opinions.
papers.limitation: Growth concentrates in Indonesia, Malaysia, and Saudi Arabia, so findings may not fit other Muslim-majority countries.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Big Data Strategies to Enhance Islamic Banks’ Competitiveness and Sustainable Development
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Islamic banks in Jordan lacked evidence on whether artificial intelligence and big data raise competitiveness and sustainable growth.
papers.fix: AI use, big data skills, and data management all linked positively to competitiveness and sustainable performance in 214 surveyed managers.
papers.practicalUseCase: AI and data work links to stronger Islamic banks, so fund it, and do not rely on staff skills alone.
papers.limitation: It is a one-time survey of Jordanian managers, so it shows links, not cause.

papers.title: ICT, High-Tech Exports, and Institutions as Drivers of Bank Expansion Growth in a Dual Banking System
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Nobody knew which factors drive bank growth in countries that have both Islamic and conventional banks.
papers.fix: Across 218 banks in 12 countries, ICT adoption drove growth most, and high-tech exports helped only when combined with ICT.
papers.practicalUseCase: Digital infrastructure drives bank growth, so governments should build it before betting on tech exports alone.
papers.limitation: Data cover 12 countries from 2010 to 2023, so findings show patterns, not proof of cause.

papers.title: Determinants of Financial Inclusion in the OIC and OECD Countries: Are They Different?
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.institution: International Centre for Education in Islamic Finance
papers.problem: Financial inclusion stays low in Muslim-majority countries despite fast growth of Islamic finance.
papers.fix: In 35 OIC and OECD countries, OIC inclusion depends on income, tertiary education, institutions, internet access, population, and age dependency.
papers.practicalUseCase: OIC countries need more digital infrastructure and support for youth and women, so aim policy there.
papers.limitation: The study covers 35 countries from 2005 to 2021 and shows links, not cause.

papers.title: Global prevalence of impostor phenomenon in medical students: A systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.institution: National University Toribio Rodríguez de Mendoza
papers.problem: Medical students face constant tests and comparison, but the global rate of impostor feelings was unknown.
papers.fix: Impostor feelings were common among medical students, though the pooled estimates varied a lot between studies.
papers.practicalUseCase: If many trainees feel like frauds, normalise it early and offer coping support in school.
papers.limitation: Results varied widely by sampling method and region, so treat the pooled figure with caution.
